passages.text: We are deceived by poverty. We become wealthy and are deceived with wealth. We are ignorant. We read and learn and are deceived with knowledge. No man is ever satisfied. That is the cause of misery, but it is also the cause of all blessing.
passages.note: Restless dissatisfaction as both misery and blessing

passages.text: A hundred years ago man walked on foot or bought horses. Now he is happy because he rides the railroad; but he is unhappy because he has to work more and earn more. Every machine that saves labour puts more stress upon labour.
passages.note: Progress and convenience bring new pressures of work

passages.text: The person for the moment on top of the wave thinks all is good; the person at the bottom says the world is [all evil]. But the man who stands aside sees the divine play going on. Some weep and others laugh. The latter will weep in their turn and the others laugh.
passages.note: Fortune rises and falls; perspective in good and bad times

passages.text: It is always for greater joy that you give up the lesser. This is practical religion — the attainment of freedom, renunciation. Renounce! Renounce the lower so that you may get the higher.
passages.note: Letting go of lesser pleasures for something higher

passages.text: Great men have died. Weak men have died. Gods have died. Death — death everywhere. This world is a graveyard of the infinite past, yet we cling to this and yet clinging to it. There is meaning in that too [because in a sense we do not die]. The mistake is that we cling to the body when it is the spirit that is really immortal.
passages.note: Facing mortality; clinging to the body

passages.text: My old Master used to say, “It is all very good to teach the parrot to say, ‘Lord, Lord, Lord’ all the time; but let the cat come and take hold of its neck, it forgets all about it” [You may] pray all the time, read all the scriptures in the world, and worship all the gods there are, [but] unless you realise the soul there is no freedom. Not talking, theorising, argumentation, but realisation. That I call practical religion.
passages.note: Faith that fails under pressure; living truth, not reciting it
